data.narrative:
Occam is a seed-stage biotech company founded by Ana Montero Horas and Andre Marques-Smith that has raised $14M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public biotech firms (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression analysis proved applicable. This method uses the $14M in total capital raised as a proxy for current value, then applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement in the sector, yielding an implied valuation of $35M. Peer-median analysis was not executable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow biotech cohort (0 matches meeting filtering criteria; methodology requires a minimum of 3 datapoints). Public-comp anchoring could not be applied because target revenue—essential for P/S multiple application—is not available; while the 3 public comps show a median P/S of 8.1x, this remains unusable without the target's revenue figure.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $30M to $40M, with a median point of $35M. This range reflects considerable uncertainty: the single applicable method dominates the calculation, and the absence of validated peer multiples or revenue data means the analysis rests substantially on stage-based mechanics rather than market-derived inputs. Revenue disclosure or identification of tighter-fit seed-stage comparables would strengthen conviction.
